Anthropic Opens Claude for Legal: 12 Practice Areas, 80+ Agents, Apache 2.0

By Will Zheng · May 16, 2026 · From Issue #11

Anthropic / GitHub / Artificial Lawyer Industry

Two weeks after publishing the financial-services repo, Anthropic shipped anthropics/claude-for-legal on May 12 — the legal-vertical analogue. The structure mirrors what they shipped for finance: 12 plugins covering specific practice areas (in-house commercial, privacy, corporate, employment, litigation, IP, regulatory, AI governance, plus law-school clinics and student learning), 80+ specialized agents (Vendor Agreement Reviewer, DSAR Responder, Claim Chart Builder, and many more), roughly 20 MCP connectors into legal-specific systems (Ironclad, Everlaw, CourtListener, Westlaw via Thomson Reuters CoCounsel), and a Managed Agents API for headless background routines. 882 stars and 165 forks in the first 24 hours. Apache 2.0 license, which means commercial use, modification, redistribution, and deployment with the firm's own API key are all permitted.

The strategic read is the same as last week's: Anthropic is converting workflow IP that took twenty years to accumulate inside top firms into a public reference implementation. The data still requires licensed seats (Westlaw, Ironclad, etc.) — the workflow does not. The "AI drafts, humans sign off" structural pattern carries over verbatim: none of the agents file documents, bind risk, or commit a firm to a position. Every output is staged for review by a qualified professional. This is precisely the design that makes adoption legally tractable in a regulated profession with bar-association exposure. With finance done two weeks ago and legal done this week, the read on Anthropic's next twelve months is clear: expect healthcare, audit/tax, and at least one more regulated vertical before year-end. The vertical-AI moat is being open-sourced, vertical by vertical, with the data connectors as the only remaining gating layer.

Sources: GitHub: anthropics/claude-for-legal · PYMNTS: Lawyers as Cowork's top users · Artificial Lawyer · Earlier knowledge-work-plugins/legal repo
